title: Add sequence-mix workload runner with delta reporting pipeline
author: Miguel Santos
release_notes: Adds a new representative workload runner (sequence-mix) and a delta reporting pipeline to compare baseline vs candidate runs. Includes new profiles, CI smoke checks, and docs. Impact: enables consistent cross-model latency/cost deltas for nightly regression detection.
description:
Motivation: We need a compact, realistic runner that replicates mixed-sequence workloads we see in production (short chats + long documents + embeddings bursts) so that nightly benchmarks surface regressions relevant to Redwood's serving optimizations. This PR introduces a sequence-mix workload runner and a small reporting pipeline that produces delta reports (baseline vs candidate) with percentile summaries and token-cost deltas.

What changed (high level):
- New runner: benchmark-lab/workloads/seq_mix_runner.py — a configurable runner that synthesizes request mixes using profile YAMLs (short/medium/long sequences, embedding bursts, chat-turn distributions).
- New reporting pipeline: benchmark-lab/reports/delta_pipeline.py — takes two result snapshots and generates a compact JSON + CSV with P50/P90/P99 deltas, token cost differences, and a per-endpoint regression flagging rule.
- Profiles: benchmark-lab/configs/seq_mix_profiles/{mobile_chat.yaml,docs_longtail.yaml,embedding_bursts.yaml}.
- CI: added ci/workflows/benchmarks.yml job to run a smoke execution of the seq-mix runner and validate the reporting pipeline.
- Tests: tests/test_seq_mix_runner.py + tests/test_delta_pipeline.py covering deterministic components and edge cases (empty runs, 1-sample baseline).
- Docs: docs/benchmarks/seq-mix.md describing how to add new profiles and interpret delta reports.

Commits summary:
- feat(runner): initial seq_mix_runner implementation with configurable distribution sampler
- test(runner): add unit tests and deterministic RNG seed harness
- feat(reports): add delta pipeline and CSV/export helper
- ci: benchmark smoke workflow and synthetic runner image
- docs: usage guide and example delta report

Files changed (high-level):
- benchmark-lab/workloads/seq_mix_runner.py
- benchmark-lab/reports/delta_pipeline.py
- benchmark-lab/configs/seq_mix_profiles/mobile_chat.yaml
- benchmark-lab/configs/seq_mix_profiles/docs_longtail.yaml
- benchmark-lab/configs/seq_mix_profiles/embedding_bursts.yaml
- tests/test_seq_mix_runner.py
- tests/test_delta_pipeline.py
- ci/workflows/benchmarks.yml
- docs/benchmarks/seq-mix.md
- Dockerfile.bench (small image to run runner)
- scripts/bench_snapshot_uploader.sh

Testing and CI: Initial CI run showed a flaky integration failure in the reporting-e2e step (timeout when uploading a ~10MB snapshot to the temporary S3-like store). I reproduced locally by shrinking the upload timeout and added exponential backoff + retry in scripts/bench_snapshot_uploader.sh. After the fix I re-triggered CI and all checks passed. See CI notes below.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Aisha Park (reviewer): "Nice isolation between runner and reporting. Two requests: (1) add a small example delta report in docs so reviewers can see expected fields, (2) please add a sane default for max_concurrent_requests in the runner config so CI doesn't accidentally hammer the dev machine."
- Miguel Santos (author): "Added example delta report and set max_concurrent_requests default to 8. Also documented the override in seq-mix.md."
- Jordan Liu (reviewer): "Could we make the per-endpoint regression threshold configurable via env var? Different customers have different sensitivities."
- Miguel Santos: "Added DELTA_REGRESSION_THRESHOLD env var and used it in delta_pipeline; default 0.15 (15% increase). Updated tests accordingly."
- Priya Menon (reviewer): "Tests look good. One nit: use pathlib in Dockerfile.bench for path joins to avoid shells on non-linux CI runners."
- Miguel Santos: "Addressed in a follow-up commit; switched to portable paths in entrypoint script."
- Priya Menon: "Approving after CI green."

CI checks and timeline:
- initial run (2026-02-21): lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (fail - report upload timeout), benchmark-smoke (skipped on first run due to timeout)
- fix pushed (2026-02-22): retry logic added to uploader script
- rerun (2026-02-24): lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), benchmark-smoke (pass), reporting-e2e (pass)
- final merge performed via squash-merge on 2026-02-28. Merge commit message condensed the feature list and noted the DELTA_REGRESSION_THRESHOLD env var.

Why this is different from the existing runners: Sequence-mix focuses on realistic cross-shape workloads (short chat-like + long doc continuation + embedding bursts) and is intentionally light-weight compared to full microburst or long-seq-only runners. The delta pipeline targets quick nightly comparisons rather than full attribution reports; it is designed to be cheap and actionable (percentile delta + cost delta + binary regression flag).

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: No breaking changes to existing benchmark artefacts. The new tools are additive. The nightly harness will be configured to run seq-mix as an optional job in the next release; ops can opt-in via bench-config.yml.

Follow-ups:
- Add a streaming mode to delta_pipeline to handle very large snapshots without materializing full JSON in memory (ENG-10012).
- Add example Linear tickets and dashboards prefilled for automated alerting when delta regression flags tripped (PERF-230).

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-28 by Miguel Santos.

If you'd like to run locally: see docs/benchmarks/seq-mix.md for quickstart; the Dockerfile.bench builds a small image with the runner and reporter plus a fixtures/ directory with sample snapshots.
